title: Seagate's new hybrid drive raises some old questions
gist: Seagate launched FireCuda Forge, a bring-your-own-SSD hybrid HDD drive managed by its new Alkemi platform, betting that AI-driven storage price inflation has revived the old hybrid-drive economics. Ars argues Seagate hasn't explained whether Alkemi caches or tiers data, the distinction that determines whether a single drive failure loses everything (Apple Fusion Drive's flaw).

insights.claim: Seagate launched the FireCuda Forge hybrid drive line in 8TB ($699) and 20TB ($899) HDD configurations that require users to supply their own SSD, its first product managed by the new Alkemi intelligent storage platform.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Seagate is pushing HDD-centric products into consumer fast storage while flash is expensive.
insights.locator: Seagate doesn’t think hybrid drives are done

insights.claim: FireCuda Forge accepts M.2 2280 NVMe SSDs (PCIe Gen3+) capped at 1TB with minimum 2,400MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write, and Seagate claims 2,500MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write for the combined USB4 system.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: 1TB fast-tier cap limits how much hot data benefits from the SSD.
insights.locator: The FireCuda Forge is available right now

insights.claim: Storage pricing per TB has exploded amid the AI boom, with some SSDs costing two to three times their historic lows according to Tom's Hardware data.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: AI demand is squeezing consumer storage supply; bullish pricing for NAND and HDD makers.

insights.claim: A Seagate Exos 24TB hard drive that sold for $298.99 in summer 2025 was priced at $699.99 by August 2026, per PCServerParts, showing mechanical drives are not immune to AI-era price inflation.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: ~134% HDD price increase in a year signals tight nearline HDD supply benefiting Seagate.
insights.locator: Mechanical drives haven’t been immune either

insights.claim: Because NAND flash remains expensive while HDDs stay cheaper per TB at high capacity, the 2026 storage cost spike revives the economic case for hybrid HDD+SSD drives that faded as SSDs got cheaper after the 2010s.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: High flash prices create product openings for HDD-led hybrid designs; reversal if NAND prices fall.
insights.quote: All storage costs have exploded, but the 2012 math still works today.
insights.locator: As solid-state storage continued getting cheaper

insights.claim: Apple's 2012 Fusion Drive tiered data in 128KB blocks across SSD and HDD, so a physical failure of either drive typically made the whole volume unrecoverable.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Block-level tiering across two devices multiplies failure risk; the benchmark against which Alkemi should be judged.
insights.locator: The problem with Apple’s Fusion solution

insights.claim: Hybrid storage failure risk hinges on caching versus tiering: Intel Smart Response Technology mirrored HDD data to the SSD with the HDD holding the authoritative copy, whereas tiering spreads unique data across both drives.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: A reusable test for any hybrid/tiered storage product: where does the authoritative copy live?

insights.claim: Seagate's Alkemi manages the storage pool from the enclosure rather than the OS, but Seagate has not disclosed whether it uses caching or tiering, how it handles a drive failure, or how it places data on first use.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Until documentation appears, data-loss risk on FireCuda Forge is unquantified; watch for Seagate technical disclosures.
